# nxeon.cloud Google discoverability collapse: analysis (2026-10-06)

Read-only analysis. Sources: nginx forensic/access logs (2026-09-22 .. 10-06, includes Host), prod DB (SELECT only), live fetches with a Googlebot UA, git log, deploy logs, journald.
Search Console data itself was not available to me; everything about Google's side is inferred from what Googlebot did to us.

## Bottom line

Nothing we serve to Googlebot is broken, and the owner's sub-sitemap theory does not fit the timeline. Googlebot got HTTP 200 on essentially every request to nxeon.cloud throughout (including after Sep 27). The cliff matches a Google-side re-evaluation of the site, most plausibly a quality/"scaled content" demotion triggered by ~65K near-templated mod pages appearing in one week (Sep 19-26), with the Sep 27 outage + full-site relaunch landing in the same 24h and muddying attribution. Bing, served the identical pages, kept crawling and indexing (about 7,480 results for site:nxeon.cloud/mods), which rules out a technical fault on our side.

## Timeline (UTC)

| When | Event |
|---|---|
| 09-19 | NxLabs mod catalogue goes live (32K mods created that day, 13K on 09-20, 18K on 09-24). |
| 09-20 14:31 (9ec9a97) | Sitemap becomes an index: /sitemap/0..5.xml (66,281 URLs: 1,431 marketing + 64,853 mods in 5 chunks of 15K). |
| 09-21 | Sitemap lastmod fix. Owner submitted numbered children in GSC (09-21, 09-26). |
| 09-24..26 | Googlebot crawls 541 / 607 / 395 mod pages per day (burst). GSC impressions peak 09-26 (~1.5K). |
| 09-27 08:21-08:31 | Root disk full, Postgres down, prod 500s (nginx: 115 5xx in the 08h bucket, 24 in the 09h bucket, all clients). Googlebot itself only saw 3 5xx that day. |
| 09-27 ~10:00 onward | Googlebot mod-page fetches drop from ~30/h to 6-20/h (before the relaunch). |
| 09-27 17:17-17:25 | .env edited (NXM_ROOT=1, NXM_LIVE=1) and nxeon-web restarted: the whole marketing site, including every /mods/* page and blog post, is now rendered by the new app/nxm templates at the same URLs. |
| 09-28 on | Googlebot mod fetches 23, 6, 0, 0, 0 per day. Non-mod Googlebot crawl continues at the normal 150-300/day. |
| 10-01 06:19 (1d483e6) | Sitemap split into named sections; mod sitemap capped (min downloads 10,000) so it lists ~18K, not 65K. |
| 10-02 04:07 (1f2ff74) | seo-014 mod quality bar deployed: failing mod pages become `noindex, follow`. About 59% of mod pages are noindex today (88 of 150 random active mods). |
| 10-02..06 | Googlebot re-reads all 11 child sitemaps; mod fetches stay at 84, 50, 27, 15, 6 per day. |

Seo policy Setting rows (`seo_*`) do not exist in prod, so all code defaults apply. There is no AuditLog history for them.

## Crawl evidence (Googlebot = 66.249.x.x only; other "Googlebot" UAs are spoofed scanners)

Googlebot requests to nxeon.cloud per day, with mod-page share and status mix:

| Day | Total | /mods/x/y pages | Non-200 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 09-22 | 258 | 126 | 7x 404, 2x 400 |
| 09-24 | 862 | 541 | 3x 404 |
| 09-25 | 924 | 607 | none |
| 09-26 | 745 | 395 | 2x 404 |
| 09-27 | 416 | 187 | 18x 400, 1x 500 |
| 09-28 | 225 | 23 | 1x 500 |
| 09-30 | 176 | 0 | 3x 404 |
| 10-02 | 312 | 82 | 4x 404 |
| 10-05 | 145 | 12 | 10x 404 (non-mod) |
| 10-06 | 325 | 6 | none |

- No 5xx, soft-404, redirect chain or robots.txt failure to Googlebot on nxeon.cloud that could explain it. (robots.txt 500/404s in the shared access log belong to kaymofilms.com / revsports.ca vhosts; nxeon.cloud robots.txt is always 200, with an occasional 301 for http or www.)
- The mod burst on 09-24..26 looks like Google's initial sampling of a newly discovered URL set; the "baseline" after it (150-300 req/day) is what Google gives this host.
- Bing: kept rising (mods 200 on 09-28, 1,672 on 10-01, 1,000-1,300/day 10-03..05). Same HTML, same sitemap. So the pages are crawlable and fetchable.
- Googlebot fetched the numbered children /sitemap/N.xml only once (3.xml, 09-23) while Bing and Ahrefs read all of them repeatedly. /sitemap.xml itself was read daily. Sitemap child fetches by Google resumed 10-02 after the rename (all 11 children, 200).

## Ranked root causes

1. **Site-wide quality/scaled-content re-evaluation by Google (confidence: medium, about 55%).**
   - 65K templated mod pages (our own audit: 28 search-referred visits across 64,853 mod pages in 30 days; 12,223 of 19,920 Minecraft mods have <80-char descriptions; descriptions copied from Modrinth/CurseForge etc.) plus about 700 game x location pages that share 81-87% of text with siblings, all appearing within about 8 days on a young domain.
   - Google crawled a sample (09-24..26), impressions spiked on exactly those days (midori-stalker: 12 clicks / 169 impressions on 09-26), then crawl demand for /mods collapsed and impressions went to about zero, including (per the owner's totals) pages that previously ranked. That pattern, plus continued normal crawling of everything else, is the classic "crawled, then dropped/deprioritised" signature.
   - Not provable from our side. Check in GSC: Pages report buckets "Crawled - currently not indexed" and "Discovered - currently not indexed" for /mods/ URLs, and the Sep 27-28 date in the indexed-pages trend.
2. **Whole-site relaunch on 09-27 17:25 plus the 08:21 outage in the same 24h (confidence: medium-low, about 30%).**
   - Every marketing URL got new HTML overnight (new templates, new copy, new nav). Google commonly re-ranks after a full re-render. The crawl slowdown on mods began 7 hours before the relaunch and right after the outage, which fits Google backing off after a burst of 5xx, but a back-off alone does not remove existing impressions.
   - I tested the new pages as Googlebot-mobile in headless Chromium: content is in the server HTML, JS-rendered content is identical, no console errors, no hidden text, title/description/canonical/robots/JSON-LD all correct, 1 h1. So the relaunch is not a technical SEO regression; at most it is a re-evaluation trigger.
3. **mod quality bar noindex + 10K sitemap floor (confidence: low as the cause of the cliff, real as an ongoing drag).** Deployed 10-01/10-02, after the cliff, so it cannot have caused it. It does mean about 114K of 194K mod pages are `noindex` now and only about 18K are in the sitemap, so the "tens of thousands of pages and none discovered" is partly by design: about 80K are indexable but unlisted, 18K listed.
4. **Page weight / TTFB (low).** Mod pages: ~230-240 KB HTML (about 51 KB gzipped), TTFB avg 0.7-0.9 s (max 4.4 s), `cache-control: no-store`. mods-1.xml/mods-2.xml take 2.0-2.6 s to generate. None of this blocks indexing but it limits Google's crawl rate for a 190K-URL host. Not a cause of the cliff (response times were similar before).

## What is NOT the cause (tested)

- **Sitemap structure.** The numbered split was 09-20 and impressions rose afterwards (peaks 09-26). The named split came 10-01/02, three to four days after the cliff. Sitemaps now validate: 11 children, 46 / 71 / 310 / 155 / 39 / 20 / 343 / 2 / 438 / 15,000 / 2,994 URLs (all under 50K/50 MB; largest 1.8 MB), 200, `application/xml`, gzip works, ttfb 0.1-2.6 s, lastmod only where real (mods 14,772 distinct, blog 341, none on templated pages). A single flat file cannot hold more than 50,000 URLs, so an index is the right structure. Google read all 11 children on 10-02 and again 10-06 with 200s; GSC "18,972 discovered pages" matches what we list (minus a few filtered).
- **robots.txt.** It already has `Sitemap: https://nxeon.cloud/sitemap.xml` (last line, after a Yandex-only `Host:` line). Allows Googlebot, disallows only dashboard/admin/api/auth. The six stale /sitemap/0..5.xml GSC entries return 200 with empty or tiny bodies or 404 by design; just delete them.
- **Indexability of listed URLs.** Of 40-60 random URLs per section: all 200, `index, follow`, self canonical (homepage canonical has no trailing slash, equivalent), no X-Robots-Tag, 1 h1, server-rendered text 3.4K-5.3K words, no hreflang (single language, correct). Exceptions: 4 game-location URLs that 404 (see fixes) and nothing else. Mod sample (120 URLs from mods-1/2): 100% 200 + indexable.
- **Internal linking.** Mod pages are linked from /mods (56 links), /mods/games/<g> (32), /mods/games/<g>/all (29 + pagination), /game-servers/mods (48), plus per-page related links. Weak point: the "all" lists expose pagination links only to ?page=2, 3 and the last page (e.g. 7131), so a crawler cannot walk 190K mods by links. Discovery is sitemap-driven. Not new on 09-27 though.
- **Duplicate/thin body.** Two mod pages share only 23% of word trigrams; about 1,200-1,400 visible words each. The thinness concern is about originality of source text (upstream copy), not boilerplate.
- **Outage as a persistent fault.** Googlebot saw 3 5xx on 09-27 and no 5xx cluster since.
- **www host / redirects.** www 301s to apex (since 10-01); no Googlebot redirect chains of note.

## Fix plan

### Code (done on branch fix/seo-discoverability, see bottom)
- Sitemap no longer lists game x location URLs whose family has no active GamePlan (they 404 under the new site): 4 L4D2 URLs today (singapore/southeast-asia/germany/europe-left-4-dead-2-server-hosting). Unit test added.

### Proposed but not implemented (need owner/product decisions or are risky)
- Do not enlarge the mod sitemap. Raising `seo_mod_sitemap_min_downloads` to 0 would re-submit ~190K near-templated URLs, which is the pattern most likely behind the demotion.
- Give mod pages unique value before asking Google for more: an original summary (install notes, compatibility matrix, "works with" and "conflicts with", real server-side status) instead of upstream copy; remove the duplicated name at the start of meta descriptions ("EssentialsX EssentialsX is...").
- Add real crawl paths: numbered/alphabetic pagination links beyond page 3 on /mods/games/<g>/all (e.g. first 10 pages + windowed), plus category hubs.
- Performance: cache mod-page HTML and the two big mod sitemaps for a few minutes (they are rebuilt per request, 2-2.6 s); drop `no-store` on anonymous mod pages. Needs a currency/geo per-route decision (as noted in docs/SEO-AUDIT-2026-10.md section 8).
- Consider stopping the `x-middleware-rewrite` response header leaking the internal /nxm path (cosmetic).

### Settings (owner decisions; my recommendation)
- Keep `seo_mod_quality_bar` on and `seo_mod_sitemap_min_downloads` at 10,000 for now, even consider lowering the listed set further (top ~5K by downloads with long descriptions) until Google shows it indexes what we already list. Fewer, better URLs rebuild trust faster than more.
- Keep `seo_gameloc_sitemap_mode` = demand. Consider `seo_gameloc_noindex_tail` = true for the 81-87% duplicate tail (about 450 pages).

### Search Console (owner)
1. Sitemaps: remove the six /sitemap/0..5.xml entries (they are dead by design). Keep /sitemap.xml only; optionally also submit the child files you want per-template coverage for (core, games, blog, mods-1, mods-2).
2. Pages report, filter by sitemap: for mods-1/mods-2 read the exact reasons ("Crawled - currently not indexed", "Discovered - currently not indexed", "Duplicate", "Alternate page with proper canonical"). That is the evidence that confirms or refutes cause 1. Also look at the Sep 27-30 range of the indexed-pages graph for a step down.
3. Manual actions and Security issues: confirm both are empty (a manual action would explain a hard cliff).
4. URL Inspection, live test + "request indexing" for: /, /game-servers, /minecraft-server-hosting, /blog, /mods/minecraft/midoris-stalker, /mods/minecraft/essentialsx. Confirm "Googlebot smartphone", "Page is indexable", and that the rendered screenshot shows content.
5. Crawl stats (Settings): compare Sep 20-26 vs Sep 28+ for host status ("Server connectivity") and average response time; a spike on 09-27 and a persistent slowdown would support the outage back-off theory.
6. Do not request indexing in bulk or resubmit large sets; wait about 2-4 weeks after changes. Recovery from a quality demotion is slow.

## Evidence files
Raw scratch (not retained): bots.log/f.log (Googlebot-only logs), sm/ (fetched sitemaps), chk.py (URL sampler).

# Google discoverability collapse on nxeon.cloud: analysis and fix (2026-10-06)

**Caveat on ANALYSIS.md:** I could not write /root/agent-notes/seo-discoverability/ANALYSIS.md. The Write tool refused because subagents must return findings as text, so the full analysis is below. Please save it there if you want the file.

## Bottom line
- **The theory doesn't fit the timeline.** Nothing we serve Googlebot is broken. The sitemap restructure is not the cause.
- **Most likely a Google-side quality or "scaled content" demotion.** About 65K near-templated mod pages appeared in a week. The outage and full-site relaunch landed in the same 24 hours and muddy the attribution.
- **Bing is a control.** It gets identical HTML and sitemaps, and kept crawling mod pages. Bing shows about 7,480 results for site:nxeon.cloud/mods. So the fault is not technical on our side.
- **Confidence is moderate, not proven.** I had no Search Console data, so Google's side is inferred from what Googlebot did to us. Nothing from our side can confirm it. Step 2 under "Owner actions in Search Console" is the check that settles it.

## Timeline (UTC)
- **09-19:** NxLabs mod catalogue goes live. 32K mods were created that day, 13K on 09-20 and 18K on 09-24.
- **09-20 14:31 (9ec9a97):** sitemap becomes an index of /sitemap/0..5.xml, 66,281 URLs (64,853 of them mods).
- **09-24 to 09-26:** Googlebot burst-crawls mod pages (541, 607 and 395 per day). GSC impressions peak on 09-26. midoris-stalker had 12 clicks and 169 impressions that day.
- **09-27 08:21 to 08:31:** root disk full, Postgres down, prod 500s. Nginx logged 115 5xx in the 08:00 hour and 24 in the 09:00 hour across all clients. Googlebot itself saw only 3 5xx that day.
- **09-27 about 10:00:** Googlebot's mod fetches fall from about 30/h to 6-20/h. This is 7 hours before the relaunch.
- **09-27 17:17 to 17:25:** NXM_ROOT=1 and NXM_LIVE=1 set in .env and nxeon-web restarted. Every marketing URL, including all mods and blog posts, is now rendered by the new app/nxm templates at the same URLs.
- **09-28 onward:** Googlebot mod fetches go 23, 6, 0, 0, 0 per day. Non-mod crawling continues at the normal 150-300 per day.
- **10-01 06:19 (1d483e6):** sitemap split into named sections. The mod sitemap is capped at 10,000 downloads, so it lists about 18K, not 65K.
- **10-02 04:07 (1f2ff74):** seo-014 mod quality bar deployed. Mod pages that fail it become `noindex, follow`.
- **No seo_* Setting rows exist in prod**, so the code defaults apply. There is no AuditLog history for them.

## Crawl evidence
Googlebot here means real 66.249.x.x only. Many other "Googlebot" UAs are spoofed scanners. The forensic log has the Host field, so I filtered to nxeon.cloud.

| Day | Total req | /mods pages | Non-200 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 09-22 | 258 | 126 | 7x 404, 2x 400 |
| 09-24 | 862 | 541 | 3x 404 |
| 09-25 | 924 | 607 | none |
| 09-26 | 745 | 395 | 2x 404 |
| 09-27 | 416 | 187 | 18x 400, 1x 500 |
| 09-28 | 225 | 23 | 1x 500 |
| 09-30 | 176 | 0 | 3x 404 |
| 10-02 | 312 | 82 | 4x 404 |
| 10-05 | 145 | 12 | 10x 404 (non-mod) |
| 10-06 | 325 | 6 | none |

- **Errors:** Googlebot got no 5xx cluster, soft-404 or redirect chain on nxeon.cloud.
- **robots.txt:** nxeon.cloud's robots.txt was always 200, with an occasional http/www 301. The 500s and 404s in the shared access log belong to the kaymofilms.com and revsports.ca vhosts.
- **The burst:** the 09-24 to 09-26 burst looks like Google sampling a newly discovered URL set. The 150-300/day afterwards is Google's baseline for this host.
- **Bing:** mods 200 on 09-28, 1,672 on 10-01, then 1,000-1,300 per day on 10-03 to 10-05.
- **Sitemap fetches:** Googlebot fetched the numbered /sitemap/N.xml files once (3.xml, 09-23). Bing and Ahrefs read them repeatedly. After the rename, Google read all 11 children on 10-02 and 10-06, all returning 200.

## Ranked root causes
1. **Google quality or scaled-content re-evaluation (about 55%, medium confidence).**
   - **The content:** our own audit (docs/SEO-AUDIT-2026-10.md) found 28 search-referred visits across 64,853 mod pages in 30 days. 12,223 of 19,920 Minecraft mods have descriptions under 80 characters, and the text is mostly upstream copy. About 700 game×location pages share 81-87% of their text with siblings.
   - **The pattern:** a young domain added all of that in about 8 days. Google sampled it, impressions spiked on those days, then mod crawl demand collapsed and impressions went to about zero. Everything else kept being crawled normally.
2. **Relaunch plus outage in the same 24 hours (about 30%).**
   - **The relaunch:** every URL got new HTML overnight, and Google commonly re-ranks after that.
   - **The outage:** it fits Google backing off after a burst of 5xx. A back-off alone doesn't remove existing impressions, though.
   - **Not a technical regression:** I rendered the pages as Googlebot-mobile in headless Chromium. Content is in the server HTML, there are no console errors and no hidden text, and title, canonical, robots, JSON-LD and h1 are all correct.
3. **Quality-bar noindex and the 10K sitemap floor (low as the cause).**
   - **Timing:** it shipped after the cliff, so it can't have caused it.
   - **Ongoing effect:** it is a real drag. 88 of 150 random active mods are noindex (about 59%, roughly 114K of 194K). About 18K mod URLs are listed in the sitemap. Roughly 80K are indexable but unlisted.
4. **Page weight and TTFB (low).**
   - **Mod pages:** about 235 KB HTML (about 51 KB gzipped), average TTFB 0.7-0.9 s with a maximum of 4.4 s, and `cache-control: no-store`.
   - **Mod sitemaps:** mods-1.xml and mods-2.xml take 2.0-2.6 s to generate.
   - **Effect:** this limits crawl rate but doesn't block indexing.

## What is NOT the cause (tested)
- **Sitemap structure:**
  - **Timing:** the numbered split was 09-20 and impressions rose afterwards. The named split was 10-01/02, after the cliff.
  - **Validity:** all 11 children are valid and under the 50K URL / 50 MB limits (largest 15,000 URLs, 1.8 MB). All return 200 with `application/xml`, and gzip works.
  - **Lastmod:** only real per-row lastmod (mods 14,772 distinct, blog 341). Templated pages have none.
  - **Flat file:** a single flat file can't hold more than 50,000 URLs, so an index is correct.
  - **Discovered count:** GSC's "18,972 discovered" matches what we list.
- **robots.txt:** it already has `Sitemap: https://nxeon.cloud/sitemap.xml` as its last line, after a Yandex-only `Host:` line. Your check missed it. It disallows only dashboard, admin, api and auth paths.
- **Indexability of listed URLs:**
  - **Sample:** I checked 40-60 random URLs per section plus 120 mod URLs, all fetched as Googlebot-mobile.
  - **Result:** all returned 200, `index, follow`, a self canonical, no X-Robots-Tag, one h1, and 3.4K-5.3K words of server-rendered text. There is no hreflang, which is correct for a single-language site.
  - **Only exception:** 4 game×location URLs that 404 (fixed below).
- **Thin boilerplate:** two mod pages share only 23% of word trigrams, with 1,200-1,400 visible words each. The concern is the originality of the upstream text, not boilerplate.
- **Internal linking:** mods are linked from /mods (56 links), /mods/games/minecraft (32), /all (29) and /game-servers/mods (48). The weak point is that pagination exposes only ?page=2, ?page=3 and the last page, so crawlers can't walk the catalogue by links. Discovery is sitemap-driven. That wasn't new on 09-27.

## What I fixed
- **Branch:** `fix/seo-discoverability`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-seofix`, commit `bd854f8b61`.
- **The fix:** `lib/sitemap-sections.ts` no longer lists game×location URLs whose family has no active GamePlan. The new site 404s those pages (`app/nxm/_data/location-game.ts`). Today that was 4 L4D2 URLs: singapore, southeast-asia, germany and europe `-left-4-dead-2-server-hosting`. If the lookup fails, the list is kept.
- **Test:** `test/sitemap-unsold-games.test.ts`.
- **Checks:** `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. The full suite has 44 failures against the 46 baseline, and I added none. The one name not in the baseline is "HARD STOP at the window's end: the running vzdump…". It is an unrelated backup-window test and looks clock-dependent (not re-run on main to confirm).
- **Not deployed or merged.**
- **No robots.txt change:** the Sitemap line already exists.
- **Not implemented** (they need product decisions or are risky):
  - more crawl paths beyond pagination page 3 on /mods/games/<g>/all
  - caching the mod pages and the two big mod sitemaps
  - dropping `no-store` on anonymous mod pages
  - removing the duplicated name at the start of mod meta descriptions ("EssentialsX EssentialsX is…")
  - the `x-middleware-rewrite` header leak

## Owner actions in Search Console
1. **Sitemaps:** delete the six /sitemap/0..5.xml entries, which are dead by design. Keep /sitemap.xml. Optionally also submit core, games, blog, mods-1 and mods-2 for per-template coverage.
2. **Pages report:** filter by the mods-1 and mods-2 sitemaps and read the exact reasons. These are "Crawled - currently not indexed", "Discovered - currently not indexed", "Duplicate" and "Alternate page with proper canonical". This is what confirms or refutes cause 1. Also look for a step down around Sep 27-30 in the indexed-pages graph.
3. **Manual actions and Security issues:** confirm both are empty, since a manual action would explain a hard cliff.
4. **URL Inspection:** run a live test and request indexing for /, /game-servers, /minecraft-server-hosting, /blog, /mods/minecraft/midoris-stalker and /mods/minecraft/essentialsx. Check that the rendered screenshot shows content.
5. **Crawl stats:** compare Sep 20-26 with Sep 28 onward for host status and average response time.
6. **No bulk requests:** don't bulk-request indexing or resubmit large sets. Give changes 2-4 weeks, because recovery from a quality demotion is slow.

## Decisions needed
- **Mod sitemap:** don't raise `seo_mod_sitemap_min_downloads` to 0. That would re-submit about 190K near-templated URLs, which is the pattern most likely behind the demotion. I'd keep the quality bar on and the 10,000 floor, and consider shrinking the listed set to roughly the top 5K mods that have long descriptions. Fewer, better URLs rebuild trust faster than more.
- **Game×location tail:** keep `seo_gameloc_sitemap_mode` at demand. Consider turning `seo_gameloc_noindex_tail` on for the roughly 450 near-duplicate tail pages.
- **Mod page uniqueness:** decide whether to invest in original per-mod value (install notes, a compatibility matrix, real server-side status) instead of relying on upstream copy. That is the only lever that addresses cause 1.

- **Errors:** Googlebot got no 5xx cluster, soft-404 or redirect chain on nxeon.cloud.

- **The burst:** the 09-24 to 09-26 burst looks like Google sampling a newly discovered URL set. The 150-300/day afterwards is Google's baseline for this host.
- **Bing:** mods 200 on 09-28, 1,672 on 10-01, then 1,000-1,300 per day on 10-03 to 10-05.
- **Sitemap fetches:** Googlebot fetched the numbered /sitemap/N.xml files once (3.xml, 09-23). Bing and Ahrefs read them repeatedly. After the rename, Google read all 11 children on 10-02 and 10-06, all returning 200.

## Ranked root causes
1. **Google quality or scaled-content re-evaluation (about 55%, medium confidence).**
   - **The content:** our own audit (docs/SEO-AUDIT-2026-10.md) found 28 search-referred visits across 64,853 mod pages in 30 days. 12,223 of 19,920 Minecraft mods have descriptions under 80 characters, and the text is mostly upstream copy. About 700 game×location pages share 81-87% of their text with siblings.
   - **The pattern:** a young domain added all of that in about 8 days. Google sampled it, impressions spiked on those days, then mod crawl demand collapsed and impressions went to about zero. Everything else kept being crawled normally.
2. **Relaunch plus outage in the same 24 hours (about 30%).**
   - **The relaunch:** every URL got new HTML overnight, and Google commonly re-ranks after that.
   - **The outage:** it fits Google backing off after a burst of 5xx. A back-off alone doesn't remove existing impressions, though.
   - **Not a technical regression:** I rendered the pages as Googlebot-mobile in headless Chromium. Content is in the server HTML, there are no console errors and no hidden text, and title, canonical, robots, JSON-LD and h1 are all correct.
3. **Quality-bar noindex and the 10K sitemap floor (low as the cause).**
   - **Timing:** it shipped after the cliff, so it can't have caused it.
   - **Ongoing effect:** it is a real drag. 88 of 150 random active mods are noindex (about 59%, roughly 114K of 194K). About 18K mod URLs are listed in the sitemap. Roughly 80K are indexable but unlisted.
4. **Page weight and TTFB (low).**
   - **Mod pages:** about 235 KB HTML (about 51 KB gzipped), average TTFB 0.7-0.9 s with a maximum of 4.4 s, and `cache-control: no-store`.
   - **Mod sitemaps:** mods-1.xml and mods-2.xml take 2.0-2.6 s to generate.
   - **Effect:** this limits crawl rate but doesn't block indexing.

## What is NOT the cause (tested)
- **Sitemap structure:**
  - **Timing:** the numbered split was 09-20 and impressions rose afterwards. The named split was 10-01/02, after the cliff.
  - **Validity:** all 11 children are valid and under the 50K URL / 50 MB limits (largest 15,000 URLs, 1.8 MB). All return 200 with `application/xml`, and gzip works.
  - **Lastmod:** only real per-row lastmod (mods 14,772 distinct, blog 341). Templated pages have none.
  - **Flat file:** a single flat file can't hold more than 50,000 URLs, so an index is correct.
  - **Discovered count:** GSC's "18,972 discovered" matches what we list.
- **robots.txt:** it already has `Sitemap: https://nxeon.cloud/sitemap.xml` as its last line, after a Yandex-only `Host:` line. Your check missed it. It disallows only dashboard, admin, api and auth paths.
- **Indexability of listed URLs:**
  - **Sample:** I checked 40-60 random URLs per section plus 120 mod URLs, all fetched as Googlebot-mobile.
  - **Result:** all returned 200, `index, follow`, a self canonical, no X-Robots-Tag, one h1, and 3.4K-5.3K words of server-rendered text. There is no hreflang, which is correct for a single-language site.
  - **Only exception:** 4 game×location URLs that 404 (fixed below).
- **Thin boilerplate:** two mod pages share only 23% of word trigrams, with 1,200-1,400 visible words each. The concern is the originality of the upstream text, not boilerplate.
- **Internal linking:** mods are linked from /mods (56 links), /mods/games/minecraft (32), /all (29) and /game-servers/mods (48). The weak point is that pagination exposes only ?page=2, ?page=3 and the last page, so crawlers can't walk the catalogue by links. Discovery is sitemap-driven. That wasn't new on 09-27.

## What I fixed
- **Branch:** `fix/seo-discoverability`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-seofix`, commit `bd854f8b61`.
- **The fix:** `lib/sitemap-sections.ts` no longer lists game×location URLs whose family has no active GamePlan. The new site 404s those pages (`app/nxm/_data/location-game.ts`). Today that was 4 L4D2 URLs: singapore, southeast-asia, germany and europe `-left-4-dead-2-server-hosting`. If the lookup fails, the list is kept.
- **Test:** `test/sitemap-unsold-games.test.ts`.
- **Checks:** `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. The full suite has 44 failures against the 46 baseline, and I added none. The one name not in the baseline is "HARD STOP at the window's end: the running vzdump…". It is an unrelated backup-window test and looks clock-dependent (not re-run on main to confirm).
- **Not deployed or merged.**
- **No robots.txt change:** the Sitemap line already exists.
- **Not implemented** (they need product decisions or are risky):
  - more crawl paths beyond pagination page 3 on /mods/games/<g>/all
  - caching the mod pages and the two big mod sitemaps
  - dropping `no-store` on anonymous mod pages
  - removing the duplicated name at the start of mod meta descriptions ("EssentialsX EssentialsX is…")
  - the `x-middleware-rewrite` header leak

## Owner actions in Search Console
1. **Sitemaps:** delete the six /sitemap/0..5.xml entries, which are dead by design. Keep /sitemap.xml. Optionally also submit core, games, blog, mods-1 and mods-2 for per-template coverage.
2. **Pages report:** filter by the mods-1 and mods-2 sitemaps and read the exact reasons. These are "Crawled - currently not indexed", "Discovered - currently not indexed", "Duplicate" and "Alternate page with proper canonical". This is what confirms or refutes cause 1. Also look for a step down around Sep 27-30 in the indexed-pages graph.
3. **Manual actions and Security issues:** confirm both are empty, since a manual action would explain a hard cliff.
4. **URL Inspection:** run a live test and request indexing for /, /game-servers, /minecraft-server-hosting, /blog, /mods/minecraft/midoris-stalker and /mods/minecraft/essentialsx. Check that the rendered screenshot shows content.
5. **Crawl stats:** compare Sep 20-26 with Sep 28 onward for host status and average response time.
6. **No bulk requests:** don't bulk-request indexing or resubmit large sets. Give changes 2-4 weeks, because recovery from a quality demotion is slow.

## Decisions needed
- **Mod sitemap:** don't raise `seo_mod_sitemap_min_downloads` to 0. That would re-submit about 190K near-templated URLs, which is the pattern most likely behind the demotion. I'd keep the quality bar on and the 10,000 floor, and consider shrinking the listed set to roughly the top 5K mods that have long descriptions. Fewer, better URLs rebuild trust faster than more.
- **Game×location tail:** keep `seo_gameloc_sitemap_mode` at demand. Consider turning `seo_gameloc_noindex_tail` on for the roughly 450 near-duplicate tail pages.
- **Mod page uniqueness:** decide whether to invest in original per-mod value (install notes, a compatibility matrix, real server-side status) instead of relying on upstream copy. That is the only lever that addresses cause 1.

## SEO discoverability fixes (2026-10-06, branch fix/seo-discoverability)

Why: Google impressions fell to ~0 from 2026-09-27 while Googlebot saw only 200s (see the analysis in the session report). The most likely cause is a quality / scaled-content re-evaluation after ~65K templated mod pages appeared in a week, so this change favours fewer, better URLs and original facts on mod pages.

- **Mod sitemap = top ~5,000 mods only.** `lib/sitemap-mods.ts` (`sitemapModCond`): active, upstream alive, not a duplicate, downloads >= `seo_mod_sitemap_min_downloads` (10,000), passes the quality bar when `seo_mod_quality_bar` is on, AND the longest of long/short description >= `seo_mod_sitemap_min_desc_chars` (default 1,000). Ranked by downloads then id, cut at `seo_mod_sitemap_max_urls` (default 5,000; 0 = no cap; clamped to 45,000). Pages outside the sitemap stay crawlable and keep their index/noindex state (the noindex policy is unchanged). The chunk is cached in memory for 15 minutes (`lib/sitemap-sections.ts`) so lastmod and content are stable between fetches and the file is fast.
- **Game x location sitemap** drops combos whose family has no active GamePlan (they 404). The tail of near-duplicate combos (location without a datacenter and without search demand, 451 of 620) is noindexed when `seo_gameloc_noindex_tail` = true (the setting already existed; default stays false until set).
- **"<Mod> on Nxeon" block** on every mod page (`lib/mod-onxeon.ts`, data in `lib/mod-onxeon-data.ts`, rendered from `app/nxm/_data/mod-lithium.ts`): one-click install support and server type, server-side flag, load rating and the smallest suggested plan (from our own rating), latest build with date, a loader x game-version table and recent builds from `ModVersion`, declared dependencies (linked when the dependency is in the catalogue), and an honest "Run this on a server" CTA. Only held facts; the block is omitted when there is too little to say. "Required by" is not shown: it needs a reverse scan of dependency JSON over ~460K builds.
- **Meta description** no longer repeats the mod name ("EssentialsX EssentialsX is...").
- **Cache headers:** `middleware.ts` + `lib/seo-cache.ts` mark anonymous mod pages (`/mods`, `/mods/games/<g>[/all]`, `/mods/<g>/<slug>`, optionally `?page=N`) `public, max-age=0, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600` with `Vary: Cookie`; any request with the session (or impersonation) cookie or an Authorization header keeps Next's private/no-store. Verify after a staging deploy with `curl -I`. The `x-middleware-rewrite` response header is added by Next's router itself; hide it in nginx with `proxy_hide_header x-middleware-rewrite;` (cosmetic).
- **Crawlable pagination:** `lib/seo-pager.ts` links first, last, neighbours and logarithmic jumps (+/-10, 100, 1,000...), so any page of a 7,000-page listing is a few hops away. Browse pages after page 1 (`/mods/games/<g>/all?page=N`) are now `noindex, follow` (the hub's `?page` already was).
- **Settings to set at deploy:** `seo_gameloc_noindex_tail` = `true`. Optional (defaults are already the recommendation): `seo_mod_sitemap_max_urls` = 5000, `seo_mod_sitemap_min_desc_chars` = 1000, `seo_mod_sitemap_min_downloads` = 10000, `seo_mod_quality_bar` = on, `seo_gameloc_sitemap_mode` = demand.

## SEO discoverability fixes (2026-10-06, branch fix/seo-discoverability)

Why: Google impressions fell to ~0 from 2026-09-27 while Googlebot saw only 200s (see the analysis in the session report). The most likely cause is a quality / scaled-content re-evaluation after ~65K templated mod pages appeared in a week, so this change favours fewer, better URLs and original facts on mod pages.

- **Mod sitemap = top ~5,000 mods only.** `lib/sitemap-mods.ts` (`sitemapModCond`): active, upstream alive, not a duplicate, downloads >= `seo_mod_sitemap_min_downloads` (10,000), passes the quality bar when `seo_mod_quality_bar` is on, AND the longest of long/short description >= `seo_mod_sitemap_min_desc_chars` (default 1,000). Ranked by downloads then id, cut at `seo_mod_sitemap_max_urls` (default 5,000; 0 = no cap; clamped to 45,000). Pages outside the sitemap stay crawlable and keep their index/noindex state (the noindex policy is unchanged). The chunk is cached in memory for 15 minutes (`lib/sitemap-sections.ts`) so lastmod and content are stable between fetches and the file is fast.
- **Game x location sitemap** drops combos whose family has no active GamePlan (they 404). The tail of near-duplicate combos (location without a datacenter and without search demand, 451 of 620) is noindexed when `seo_gameloc_noindex_tail` = true (the setting already existed; default stays false until set).
- **"<Mod> on Nxeon" block** on every mod page (`lib/mod-onxeon.ts`, data in `lib/mod-onxeon-data.ts`, rendered from `app/nxm/_data/mod-lithium.ts`): one-click install support and server type, server-side flag, load rating and the smallest suggested plan (from our own rating), latest build with date, a loader x game-version table and recent builds from `ModVersion`, declared dependencies (linked when the dependency is in the catalogue), and an honest "Run this on a server" CTA. Only held facts; the block is omitted when there is too little to say. "Required by" is not shown: it needs a reverse scan of dependency JSON over ~460K builds.
- **Meta description** no longer repeats the mod name ("EssentialsX EssentialsX is...").
- **Cache headers:** `middleware.ts` + `lib/seo-cache.ts` mark anonymous mod pages (`/mods`, `/mods/games/<g>[/all]`, `/mods/<g>/<slug>`, optionally `?page=N`) `public, max-age=0, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600` with `Vary: Cookie`; any request with the session (or impersonation) cookie or an Authorization header keeps Next's private/no-store. Verify after a staging deploy with `curl -I`. The `x-middleware-rewrite` response header is added by Next's router itself; hide it in nginx with `proxy_hide_header x-middleware-rewrite;` (cosmetic).
- **Crawlable pagination:** `lib/seo-pager.ts` links first, last, neighbours and logarithmic jumps (+/-10, 100, 1,000...), so any page of a 7,000-page listing is a few hops away. Browse pages after page 1 (`/mods/games/<g>/all?page=N`) are now `noindex, follow` (the hub's `?page` already was).
- **Settings to set at deploy:** `seo_gameloc_noindex_tail` = `true`. Optional (defaults are already the recommendation): `seo_mod_sitemap_max_urls` = 5000, `seo_mod_sitemap_min_desc_chars` = 1000, `seo_mod_sitemap_min_downloads` = 10000, `seo_mod_quality_bar` = on, `seo_gameloc_sitemap_mode` = demand.
E

- sitemap: quality gate (description length) + cap by downloads, in-memory chunk cache
- mod pages: install/compat/dependency/build facts from our data; meta description dedupes the name

input.message:
All four items are implemented on `fix/seo-discoverability` (worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-seofix`) as commit `f518dd9b88` on top of `bd854f8b61`. I did not deploy or merge, and prod DB use was SELECT-only.

**What I checked**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- I ran the targeted tests only (47 pass, 0 fail): the new `test/mod-onxeon.test.ts` (8 tests), `sitemap-unsold-games`, `mod-quality`, `seo-audit` and `bot-classify`.
- I skipped the full suite and `next build`: available memory dipped to 2 GB mid-task and I never saw 12 GB free. The earlier full-suite run on `bd854f8` had 44 failures against the 46-name baseline.
- I did not render the new mod-page block or fetch the new headers on a running server (no build or dev server, to save memory). The block and the cache header are therefore verified only by unit tests and type-checking.

**Commit contents**
1. **Mod sitemap, quality over quantity** (`lib/sitemap-mods.ts`, `lib/seo-index-policy.ts`, `lib/sitemap-sections.ts`):
   - The sitemap now lists a mod only if it is active, upstream still exists, and is not a duplicate. It must also have at least 10,000 downloads, pass the quality bar, and have a long or short description of at least 1,000 characters.
   - Survivors are ranked by downloads and cut at 5,000 URLs. The rest stay crawlable and keep whatever index/noindex state they have today.
   - The chosen threshold is from the data: 35,216 mods have at least 10,000 downloads and a description of at least 1,000 characters, so the cap of 5,000 is what decides the list.
   - Each file is cached in memory for 15 minutes, so lastmod stays stable between fetches and the file is fast. It was 2–2.6 s per file.
   - Mod noindex rules are unchanged: nothing new is noindexed on mod pages.
2. **Original facts on mod pages**:
   - Every mod page gets a "<Mod> on Nxeon" block (`lib/mod-onxeon.ts`, `lib/mod-onxeon-data.ts`, wired in `app/nxm/_data/mod-lithium.ts`), built only from data we hold.
   - It shows whether one-click install is supported and which server type, the server-side flag, our load rating, and the smallest plan we suggest from that rating.
   - It also shows the latest build and date, a loader × game-version table, recent builds from `ModVersion`, and dependencies (linked when the dependency is in our catalogue).
   - It ends with a "Run this on a server" CTA, and the block is omitted when we hold too little to say.
   - The meta description no longer repeats the mod name ("EssentialsX EssentialsX is…").
   - "Required by" is not shown: it would need a reverse scan of dependency JSON across about 460K builds.
3. **Speed and crawl**:
   - `middleware.ts` and `lib/seo-cache.ts` send `public, max-age=0, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600` plus `Vary: Cookie` on anonymous mod pages. These are `/mods`, `/mods/games/<g>`, `/mods/games/<g>/all` and `/mods/<g>/<slug>`, plus `?page=N`.
   - Any request with the session or impersonation cookie, or an Authorization header, keeps Next's private no-store. Next honours a middleware-set Cache-Control (it only sets its own when none exists).
   - Pagination (`lib/seo-pager.ts`) now links first, last, neighbours and ±10/100/1000 jumps. A test shows any page of a 7,131-page listing is at most 6 hops from page 1. It is on `/mods/games/<g>/all` and the `/mods` hub.
   - Browse pages after page 1 (`/mods/games/<g>/all?page=N`) are now `noindex, follow`. The hub's `?page` already was.
4. **Game × location tail**: the setting `seo_gameloc_noindex_tail` already existed and the sitemap mode already defaults to demand, so I made no code change. 451 of 620 combos are tail pages and would be noindexed once the setting is on.
5. I appended a section to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

**Sitemap URL counts, from a read-only run against the prod DB with the new code**

| Section | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| core | 46 | 46 |
| games | 71 | 71 |
| game-locations | 310 | 306 (the 4 that 404 are gone, from `bd854f8`) |
| locations | 155 | 155 |
| compare | 39 | 39 |
| tools | 20 | 20 |
| blog | 343 | 343 |
| servers | 2 | 2 |
| directory | 438 | 439 |
| mods-1 | 15,000 | 5,000 |
| mods-2 | 2,993 | removed |
| **Total** | **19,409** | **6,421** |

**Newly noindexed**
- Mod pages: none.
- Browse pages after page 1: about 16K listing pages, roughly 194K mods ÷ 12 per page across families. They stay crawlable and followed.
- Game × location: 451 pages, only if you set `seo_gameloc_noindex_tail` to true.

**Settings to set at deploy**
- Required: `seo_gameloc_noindex_tail` = `true`.
- Optional, because the defaults already match the recommendation: `seo_mod_sitemap_max_urls` = 5000, `seo_mod_sitemap_min_desc_chars` = 1000, `seo_mod_sitemap_min_downloads` = 10000, `seo_mod_quality_bar` = on, `seo_gameloc_sitemap_mode` = demand.
- Setting `seo_mod_sitemap_max_urls` to 0 removes the cap, which is the opposite of the recommendation.

**Things I'm unsure about**
- **Cache header:** after a staging deploy, check `curl -I` with and without a session cookie. If Next overrides the header, the fallback is nginx `proxy_cache`, which needs a prod nginx change.
- **`x-middleware-rewrite` leak:** Next's router adds it, so it can't be removed in app code. Use `proxy_hide_header x-middleware-rewrite;` in nginx. It is cosmetic.
- **Page-1 duplication:** the first browse page is still indexable and the `?page=N` URLs are noindexed, which I think is right.
- **Sitemap description gate:** it counts upstream text, so it is a proxy for substance. The original value comes from the new on-page block. The mod sitemap is a single file now, and the numbered ids are still 404 by design.

**ANALYSIS.md not saved:** the Write tool refused to save `/root/agent-notes/seo-discoverability/ANALYSIS.md`, so the analysis is only in my earlier report, not on disk.
